events.summary: STORY: Unionized workers at South Korea's Kakao staged a four-hour strike and rally on Wednesday.They demanded job security and changes to the tech firm's bonus system. Hundreds of workers wearing black T-shirts and holding white umbrellas walked out of Kakao's office in the morning.The union had told police as many as 1,200 members would join the rally.Local media reported the union plans a general strike for June 29 with all 5,000 members due to take part.Kakao operates South Korea's biggest messaging app by users, and employs about 6,000 people.The dispute comes with growing labor unrest in South Korea as tech firms score record earnings during the global AI boom.Samsung Electronics' union got ⁠a ​deal this month tying chip division bonuses to ​10.5% of operating profit.Kakao said last month it had failed to reach a wage deal with the union in government-mediated talks.The union wants reform to Kakao's compensation system.They argue executives have received higher bonus payments in recent years while other employees have seen limited benefits.Kakao previously said it turned down a union demand for profit-sharing, calling it unrealistic.The union refused to confirm details on the negotiation.Kakao said Wednesday its running a real-time system in response to the strike.It added management will keep talking with the union.

events.summary: South Korea's Kakao Corp union said on Monday it will stage a four-hour strike ‌and rally in Pangyo on June 10, demanding job ‌security and reforms to a compensation system it says disproportionately rewards executives. The move ⁠comes after government-mediated wage talks broke down last week, with Kakao rejecting union demands — including profit-sharing proposals — as unrealistic and "a big ​burden" on ​management as it prioritises investment ​and shareholder returns.

events.summary: Deutsche Bank strategists, led by Parag Thatte, warn of stock market volatility around Federal Reserve policy meetings, especially during rapid rate hikes. events.summary: Energy inflation is no longer solely driven by crude oil prices but also by tight supplies of refined products, leading to an unusual divergence where crude prices ease while refined fuel prices rise. This "crack spread" indicates that inflationary pressures are stemming from supply constraints in products like gasoline and diesel, potentially keeping overall inflation elevated even if crude oil prices fall. The persistence of high energy prices could lead to more restrictive monetary policies, though central bank actions may vary based on regional growth outlooks, creating opportunities in global fixed income.
events.title: The Crack in the Oil Story: Unpacking Inflation Persistence

events.summary: RTX Corporation (NYSE:RTX) is a major aerospace and defense company listed on the S&P 500, operating through its three principal units: Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon. events.summary: Cummins (CMI) generated a 512% return over the last decade, transforming a $1,000 investment into $6,120, but its dividend growth was even more remarkable, increasing for 17 consecutive years from $0.175 to $2.20 per quarter, even through economic downturns.
